concepts.name: Functions of several variables
concepts.summary: Recognise and evaluate functions of two or three inputs and describe their domain and range.

concepts.name: Graphs and level curves
concepts.summary: Interpret a surface z=f(x,y) and its level curves to read how the function changes.

concepts.name: Vectors in 2D and 3D
concepts.summary: Represent points and displacements as vectors and compute their sums, scalar multiples and lengths.

concepts.name: Dot and cross products
concepts.summary: Explain what the dot product (angle, projection) and cross product (perpendicular vector, area) measure.

concepts.name: Partial derivative meaning
concepts.summary: Explain a partial derivative as the rate of change in one variable while the others are held fixed.

concepts.name: Lines and planes in space
concepts.summary: Describe lines and planes in 3D using parametric and normal-vector equations.

misconceptions.text: A partial derivative with respect to x measures the total change of the function as all variables change.
The cross product of two vectors is a number, like the dot product.
Level curves of a function are the same as its cross-sections by vertical planes.

concepts.name: Computing partial derivatives
concepts.summary: Calculate first and second partial derivatives, including mixed partials, by treating other variables as constants.

concepts.name: Tangent planes and linearisation
concepts.summary: Find the tangent plane to a surface at a point and use it to approximate function values.

concepts.name: Gradient vector
concepts.summary: Compute the gradient and state that it points in the direction of steepest increase and is normal to level curves.

concepts.name: Directional derivatives
aliases: rate of change along a vector
concepts.summary: Compute the rate of change in any unit direction as the dot product of the gradient with that direction.

concepts.name: Iterated double integrals
concepts.summary: Evaluate double integrals over rectangles and simple regions as iterated single integrals.

concepts.name: Parametric curves in space
concepts.summary: Describe curves by vector functions r(t) and compute their tangent vectors and arc length.

concepts.name: Multivariable chain rule
concepts.summary: Apply the chain rule to composite functions using tree diagrams to find derivatives with respect to underlying variables.

misconceptions.text: The gradient is a scalar giving the slope of the function.
The directional derivative does not depend on whether the direction vector is a unit vector.
A double integral can be computed with the order of integration swapped without changing the limits, even over non-rectangular regions.

concepts.name: Optimisation with second-derivative test
concepts.summary: Find critical points and classify them as maxima, minima or saddles using the second-derivative test.

concepts.name: Lagrange multipliers
concepts.summary: Solve constrained extremum problems by setting the gradient of the objective parallel to the gradient of the constraint.

concepts.name: Double integrals over general regions
concepts.summary: Set up limits for non-rectangular regions and choose or reverse the order of integration.

concepts.name: Polar coordinate integration
concepts.summary: Convert a double integral to polar form including the factor r in dA.

concepts.name: Triple integrals
concepts.summary: Set up and evaluate triple integrals for volumes and masses over 3D regions.

concepts.name: Cylindrical and spherical coordinates
concepts.summary: Choose a suitable coordinate system for a region and convert integrals with the correct volume element.

concepts.name: Vector fields and divergence-curl
concepts.summary: Sketch vector fields and compute their divergence and curl.

misconceptions.text: A point where all partial derivatives are zero is always a local maximum or minimum.
Converting to polar coordinates only requires substituting x=r cosθ and y=r sinθ, with dA becoming dr dθ.
In spherical coordinates the volume element is simply dρ dφ dθ.

concepts.name: Change of variables with Jacobians
concepts.summary: Analyse a transformation, compute its Jacobian determinant and use it to rewrite integrals over a simpler region.

concepts.name: Line integrals
concepts.summary: Evaluate line integrals of scalar and vector fields along parametrised curves and interpret them as mass or work.

concepts.name: Conservative fields and potentials
concepts.summary: Test whether a field is conservative, find a potential function and use it to evaluate line integrals.

concepts.name: Green's theorem
concepts.summary: Relate a line integral around a closed plane curve to a double integral and apply it in either direction.

concepts.name: Parametric surfaces and surface area
concepts.summary: Parametrise surfaces and compute normal vectors and area through the cross product of tangent vectors.

concepts.name: Surface integrals and flux
concepts.summary: Evaluate scalar surface integrals and flux of a vector field through oriented surfaces.

concepts.name: Stokes' and divergence theorems
concepts.summary: Apply Stokes' and the divergence theorem, judging when each simplifies a computation and checking orientation and hypotheses.

misconceptions.text: The Jacobian factor is just the product of the partial derivatives, with no determinant needed.
A field is conservative whenever the line integral is zero around one particular closed curve.
Green's theorem applies to any closed curve regardless of orientation or singularities inside the region.

concepts.name: Unifying integral theorems
concepts.summary: Evaluate how the fundamental theorem, Green's, Stokes' and divergence theorems are instances of one boundary-integral principle.

concepts.name: Domain topology and closed versus exact fields
concepts.summary: Judge how holes in a domain make curl-free fields non-conservative, as with the circulation of the angular field around the origin.

concepts.name: Curvilinear coordinates and scale factors
concepts.summary: Derive gradient, divergence, curl and Laplacian in arbitrary orthogonal coordinates using scale factors.

concepts.name: Conservation laws from theorems
concepts.summary: Derive integral and differential forms of physical laws such as continuity, Gauss's and Faraday's laws from the integral theorems.

concepts.name: Constrained optimisation analysis
concepts.summary: Evaluate second-order conditions and inequality constraints for multivariable optimisation and interpret multipliers as sensitivities.

concepts.name: Validity and regularity conditions
concepts.summary: Critique when interchanging integrals, differentiating under the integral, or applying theorems fails due to singularities or lack of smoothness.

concepts.name: Modelling with fields and integrals
concepts.summary: Construct a multivariable model, choose coordinates and theorems, and design an efficient solution for a physical problem.

misconceptions.text: Zero curl on a domain is always enough for path independence, whatever the domain's shape.
The Laplacian and divergence in curvilinear coordinates are found by just replacing x,y,z with the new coordinates in the Cartesian formulas.
Iterated integrals can always be swapped in order if the integrand is defined everywhere.
